edges.label: same_fact
edges.reason: Both quotes state a cost of $4.3 billion for the telescope. Source origin and time action are not explicitly established within the quotes themselves.

edges.sentence: On 2026-08-29, CBS News reported “the telescope will still cost taxpayers some $4.3 billion to build, launch and operate for its five-year primary mission.”; on 2026-08-30, CBS News reported “NASA 's $4.3 billion Roman Space Telescope was launched atop a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket Sunday, kicking off a three-month voyage to a point in space a million miles from Earth where it will map the large-scale structure of the cosmos with a wide-field 300-megapixel camera.”.

new_slots.name: launch time
new_slots.sentence: The long-awaited flight got underway at 7:26 a.m. EDT when the Falcon Heavy's three core stages, each powered by nine kerosene-burning Merlin engines, roared to life, throttled up to more than five million pounds of thrust and majestically climbed away from historic Pad 39A at the Kennedy Space Center.

new_slots.name: Falcon Heavy flights
new_slots.sentence: It was only the 13th flight of a Falcon Heavy, the most powerful operational rocket in the SpaceX inventory, and it provided a spectacular weekend sky show for area residents, tourists and space center workers as it rapidly raced away on an easterly trajectory over the Atlantic Ocean.

new_slots.name: telescope mass
new_slots.sentence: A SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket carrying NASA's Roman Space Telescope was hauled to pad 39A at the Kennedy Space Center overnight Friday to set the stage for launch.

new_slots.name: L2 distance
new_slots.sentence: The observatory is bound for Lagrange Point No. 2, about a million miles on the opposite side of Earth from the sun, where the gravity of the Earth and sun balance out, allowing spacecraft to remain in place with minimal use of fuel.

new_slots.name: solar panel status
new_slots.sentence: Shortly after, the telescope's solar panels unfolded as planned.

new_slots.name: booster separation time
new_slots.sentence: The rocket's two strap-on side boosters, one making its first flight and the other its third, shut down and peeled away 2 1/2 minutes after liftoff.

new_slots.name: spacecraft release time
new_slots.sentence: The 18,000-pound Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, named after NASA's first chief astronomer who long championed the value of space-based telescopes, was released to fly on its own 31 minutes after liftoff.

new_slots.name: exoplanets discovered
new_slots.sentence: About 6,200 exoplanets have been discovered to date using smaller instruments like NASA's Kepler Space Telescope.

new_slots.name: mirror mass
new_slots.sentence: The solar-powered Roman is built around a 7.9-foot-wide, 410-pound primary mirror — one of two donated to NASA by the National Reconnaissance Office
